blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Films introduce characters incrementally as they progress. We study the problem of identifying principal characters and assigning their names directly from the movie itself, without using external cast lists, actor photographs, or pre-built character banks. We introduce the character naming task: given a name mentioned in dialogue and the associated video context, the model must determine which visible character bears that name. This task is challenging because name resolution often depends on cinematic cues such as shot-reverse-shot structure, self-introduction, direct address, third-party reference, gaze, and temporal continuity. We provide a dataset and annotations for evaluating character naming and first character appearances, develop a video-and-dialogue model for the task, and compare it with proprietary multimodal large language models. We further introduce a progressive framework for building a character bank as the film unfolds. Together, these contributions support online, human-like movie understanding in which character identities are inferred from the film itself.
blocks.zh: 电影随着进步逐步引入人物. 我们研究识别主角和直接从电影中指定他们的名字的问题,而不使用外部的铸造名单,演员照片,或者预先建造的角色库. 我们介绍角色命名任务:给对话中提到的一个名字以及相关的视频上下文,模型必须确定哪个可见的人物带有这个名字. 这项工作具有挑战性,因为名称分辨率往往取决于电影提示,例如镜头反射结构、自我引入、直接地址、第三方参考、视线和时间连续性。 我们提供一个数据集和说明,用于评价角色命名和第一角色外观,为任务开发视频和对话模型,并与专有的多模式大型语言模型进行比较. 随着电影的展开,我们进一步引入了建设人物库的渐进框架. 这些贡献共同支持在线,人相类的电影理解,其中人物身份是从电影本身推断出来的.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The objective of this paper is to watch a film as a human would – ingesting the film frame-by-frame in an online mode,
and identifying the principal characters and their names as the story unfolds . Traditional films, such as a romantic comedy,
consist of characters and their story arcs. In order for the viewer to quickly understand who these principal characters are, the
film must introduce and name them towards the start of the film. This is achieved by a combination of cinematic devices (such as the camera following the person, and close-ups) and using the dialogue or other information to name them, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en: Obtaining character names explicitly only from the film is in stark contrast to the methods employed recently in the literature for tasks like generating audio descriptions and transcripts [ 43 , 25 , 24 , 26 , 68 , 67 , 21 ] . In these works, a character bank is first constructed using a cast list and actor photos from IMDB, Fandom and other online sources. The character bank is then used to label the principal characters throughout the film using face recognition (or voice recognition for animated films [ 21 ] ).

blocks.en:
To operationalize our goal, we first investigate how the viewer is
presented with the name of a character as they watch the film –
almost always it is from the dialogue, and very occasionally from
other sources, such as name badges. This enables the character naming task to be automated and evaluated – given a name in
the dialogue, the associated shots can be used to ask the question:
which of the people appearing in this clip has this name? To this end,
the first contribution of this paper is to build a dataset from
MovieNet [ 28 ] and Movie101 [ 73 ] films that can be used to train and evaluate this
task. We develop a method to solve this task, using the video and
dialogue, and compare its performance to proprietary Multimodal LLMs
(MLLMs), such as Gemini [ 19 ] . This is a challenging task, as correct
inference often requires an understanding of film editing style (as
the person addressed by name may be shown in a different shot) and
also character gaze and eyeline (to know who they are looking at when
saying a name).

blocks.en:
This establishes that characters can be named in films, using the information presented by the screenwriter and director. Often, the name of a principal character is presented multiple times across different dialogues throughout the film, providing opportunities for error correction (by both human and machine) if the first presentation had been missed or incorrectly assigned.
Once the principal characters are named (possibly multiple times), they can be recognized throughout the rest of the movie, and retrospectively named from their first appearance (using human or machine memory).
To this end, we introduce two further tasks: (i) annotating the movies with the first appearance of the principal characters (which may well be before they are named in the dialogue); and (ii) progressively building up a character bank as the film progresses. The character bank records the appearance, voice and names of the principal characters (as in previous work). We provide annotations to evaluate the character first appearance over a number of movies. For example, in the movie Juno , the protagonist Juno is introduced in the first shot of the film, and appears in almost every scene, but is not named until 7.2 7.2 minutes into the film.

为此,我们提出另外两项任务: (一)用主角的首次出现来注释电影(很可能在对话中命名之前); (二)随着电影的发展逐步建立角色库. 人物库记录主角的外表,声音和姓名(和前作一样). 我们提供说明来评价角色 首次出现在一些电影。 例如,在电影"朱诺"中,主角朱诺在电影的第一镜头中被引入,并出现在几乎每个场景中,但直到电影进入7.2.7.2分钟后才被命名.

blocks.en:
In summary, we make the following four contributions:
(i) we introduce the new task of character naming from dialogue alone, a key enabling step for watching and understanding a film as a human does; (ii) we provide the Movie Character Naming (MCN) dataset with 23,792 23,792 instances of multiple-choice character naming over 407 407 movies, and also 20 20 movies with the first appearance of the principal characters annotated; (iii)
we develop a character naming model using open-source MLLMs, and compare its performance to proprietary MLLMs, analysing what is difficult to solve; and (iv)
we introduce the first automatic method to progressively build up a character bank for a feature-length movie. These capabilities put in place the foundation for understanding character arcs and, ultimately, the story of a film.
The dataset and models are available at: https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/StreamCast/ .

blocks.en: 2 Movie Character Naming (MCN) Dataset
blocks.zh: 2 电影字符命名( MCN) 数据集

blocks.en: In this section, we introduce the Movie Character Naming (MCN) Dataset, which provides annotations for two complementary tasks: Character Naming and First Occurrence . The Character Naming annotations consist of video segments in which character names are uttered in the dialogue, each paired with ground-truth name-to-track mappings. The First Occurrence annotations, by contrast, are designed to evaluate the streaming pipeline for character bank construction, and provide two (possibly coinciding) timestamps per principal character: the moment they first appear on screen, and the moment their name is first revealed.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们介绍电影字符命名(MCN)数据集,该数据集为两个互补任务提供了说明:字符命名和第一次出现. "字符命名说明"由视频段组成,其中角色名称在对话中发音,每段都配对地面真实的名称到轨道映射. 相比之下,第一事件说明旨在评价字符库建设的流线管道,并按主角提供两个(可能同时出现的)时间戳:它们首次出现在屏幕上的那一刻,以及它们的名字被首次披露的时刻.

Additional examples are provided in Appendix H . In the following, we first describe how the dataset is annotated given character tracks and dialogue. The implementation details for obtaining the character face-tracks and dialogue are given in Sec. 2.3 .

blocks.en: 2.1 Data Collection and Curation
blocks.zh: 2.1 数据收集和校正

blocks.en: We build MCN on top of MovieNet [ 28 ] and Movie101 [ 73 ] , which already provide ground-truth mappings between character names and body bounding-box coordinates.
blocks.zh: 我们在MovieNet[28]和Movie101[73]上架MCN,它们已经提供了人物名称和身体边框坐标之间的地面真实图.

blocks.en: Annotations for Character Naming (CN). We construct the associations between character names and face tracks in three steps. First, since MovieNet and Movie101 already provide ground-truth name–body associations, we align character body boxes with their face tracks in space and time, yielding name–face associations for all characters appearing on screen. Second, we keep only those associations whose corresponding names are also mentioned in the dialogue, since these are the only ones inferable from the audio–visual signal we use. Third, we handle the case where a name is mentioned in the dialogue but the corresponding face track is unavailable (e.g., when the character is referred to in absentia). In this case, we label the association as none , since no in-clip cues support the assignment. As a result, we provide the final name–face associations as ground-truth labels, along with all character-level face tracks in the video clip as candidate options, to construct a multiple-choice instance.
blocks.zh: 字符命名说明 (CN). 我们分三个步骤构建人物名称和面孔的关联. 首先,由于MovieNet和Movie101已经提供了地面真名-body关联,因此我们在空间和时间上将字符体框与他们的面轨对齐,产生屏幕上所有字符的名称-face关联。 第二,我们只保留那些在对话中也提到相应名称的社团,因为这些社团是我们使用的视听信号中唯一可以推断的。 第三,我们处理在对话中提及某个名字但相应的面孔音轨无法使用的案件(例如,在缺席中提及该字符时)。 在此情况下,我们称协会为无,因为没有内切提示支持任务. 因此,我们提供了最终名称-面部协会作为地面真实标签,以及视频片段中所有字符级面部音轨作为候选选项,以构建一个多选择实例。

blocks.en: Annotations for First Occurrence (FO). For every character in the movie, we manually annotate two timestamps: the first visual occurrence , i.e. the moment the character first appears on screen, and the first naming , i.e. the moment at which a human viewer can first associate the character’s visual appearance with their name based solely on the preceding content.
blocks.zh: 第一次出现说明。 对于电影中的每一个角色,我们手动注释了两个倍数:第一个视觉事件,即角色首次出现在屏幕上的那一刻,第一个命名,即人类观众可以先将角色的视觉外观与仅基于前述内容的名字联系起来的时刻.

blocks.en: Quality Control. To ensure a high-quality test set, we manually inspect every test sample and correct errors in face-track clustering and name labelling. We then run state-of-the-art proprietary models on the curated set and examine cases where their outputs disagree with the annotation, fixing any remaining errors (or confirming the annotation is correct but the model fails).
blocks.zh: 质检. 为了确保高质量的测试集,我们手动检查每个测试样本,并纠正面轨集群和名称标签的错误. 然后,我们运行最先进的专有模式在所编集上,并检查其产出与注释不一致的情况,纠正任何剩余的错误(或确认注释是正确的,但模型失败).

blocks.en: 2.3 Preprocessing – Character-Level Face-Tracks and Associated Speech
blocks.zh: 2.3 预处理 - 字符级面架和相关发言

blocks.en: To obtain multiple-choice instances for Character Naming , we need to extract character-level tracks and speech from video clips around name occurrences in the dialogue, therefore enabling us to ask models to select one of them for each query name. This involves extracting a face-track cluster f i f_{i} for each character and linking it with the corresponding voice-track cluster v j v_{j} . Note, this pre-processing is done at the clip level when annotating the dataset, but results are also made available over the entire movie for downstream tasks (e.g., character bank construction).
blocks.zh: 为了获得字符命名的多个选择实例,我们需要从对话框中的名称事件周围的视频剪辑中提取字符级别音轨和语音,从而使我们能够要求模型为每个查询名称选择其中之一. 这涉及为每个字符提取一个face-track croup f i f_{i}并将其与相应的语音-track croup v j v_{j}连接起来. 注意,这种预处理在对数据集进行注释时在剪辑级别进行,但结果也在整个电影中为下游任务提供(如人物银行构造).

blocks.en: Face Track Extraction. For each recurring character i i , we detect and track faces across shots and group the tracks into a character-level face-track cluster f i f_{i} . The detailed procedure is given in Appendix A.1 .
blocks.zh: 脸孔追踪提取器。 对于每个反复出现的字符 i i, 我们检测和跟踪面孔 通过镜头, 并将轨道分组到一个字符级的面孔轨道 集群 f i f_{i}。 详细程序见附录A.1。

blocks.en: Linking Voices to Face Tracks. For the clean voice segments in the video, we first apply speaker diarization to group them into voice clusters, with each cluster denoted v j v_{j} . To match each voice cluster to an existing face track (i.e. to identify who is speaking on screen), we apply TalkNet [ 57 ] to obtain synchronization scores s i , j s_{i,j} between faces f i f_{i} and voices v j v_{j} . Each voice cluster is then assigned to the face-track cluster with the highest synchronization score, yielding complete character identities with paired faces and voices.
blocks.zh: 将声音链接到 Face Tracks 。 对于视频中干净的语音部分,我们首先应用扬声器的对称化将其组合成语音集群,每个集群表示v j v_{j}. 为了将每个语音集群匹配到一个已有的面音轨(即识别谁在屏幕上说话),我们应用TalkNet [57]来获得在face f i , j s_{i, j}和 voice v j v_{j}之间的同步分数. 每个语音集群随后被分配到同步分数最高的面轨集群,产生配对面和声音的完整字符身份.

blocks.en:
As a further preprocessing step, we transcribe the voice tracks into textual dialogue with Parakeet [ 47 ] . Since each voice track is linked to a face cluster, this naturally yields visually grounded subtitles.
Finally, the character names n n emerge as a natural by-product of subtitle extraction. We retain clips whose subtitles contain at least one character name, passing them to the subsequent character naming step.
blocks.zh:
作为进一步的预处理步骤,我们将语音音轨转换成与Parakeet [47] 的文字对话. 由于每个语音音轨都与一个面团相连,这自然会产生视网膜字幕.
最后,人物名称nn出现为字幕提取的自然副产品. 我们保留了字幕至少包含一个字符名的片段,将其传递到之后的字符命名步骤.

blocks.en: 3 Assigning Names to Characters
blocks.zh: 3 指定字符名称

blocks.en:
The task of assigning names to characters, i.e., Character Naming (CN),
is performed naturally by humans while watching a film, but is not trivial for deep learning systems owing to multiple challenges: first, a character may be addressed directly by name, or referred to in the third person while off-screen, or revealed only through what others say about them; second, who is being addressed may only be indicated by gaze or by the editing structure, for example, as one character says a name, and the named character then reacts in the subsequent shot. We therefore treat CN as a new multimodal task that requires joint reasoning over textual cues (e.g., conversational logic, vocative address) and visual cues (e.g., eye contact, on-screen presence).
blocks.zh:
指定字符的任务,即字符命名(CN),
由人类在观看电影时自然表演,但由于多重挑战,对于深层学习系统来说并不是微不足道的:第一,一个角色可能直接通过名字处理,或者在外屏时在第三人称中被提及,或者只能通过其他人对其的描述来揭示;第二,正在处理的人只能通过目光或编辑结构来表示,例如,一个角色说出一个名字,被命名的人物随后在镜头中反应. 因此,我们把CN视为一项新的多式联运任务,它要求对文字提示(如对话逻辑、促动地址)和视觉提示(如眼睛接触、屏幕上的存在)进行联合推理。

blocks.en: In this section, we first describe how we operationalize Character Naming for MLLMs through visual prompting alone (Sec. 3.1 ). We then introduce a fine-tuning recipe that improves the MLLMs’ reasoning on this task, enabling more reliable assignments of character names (Sec. 3.2 ).
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们首先描述我们如何单独通过视觉提示操作MLLMs的字符命名(第3.1节)。 然后,我们采用了一种微调的配方,改进MLLMs对这项任务的推理,从而能够更可靠地指派角色(第3.2节)。

blocks.en: 3.1 MLLM-Based Character Naming
blocks.zh: 3.1 基于 MLLM 字符 命名

blocks.en: To adapt MLLMs for character naming in a zero-shot manner, we use the following prompting strategies.
blocks.zh: 为了以零镜头的方式调整MLLMs的字符命名,我们使用以下的提示策略.

blocks.en: Prompting the MLLM with Visual Identities. Rather than providing the MLLM with bounding-box coordinates of the face tracks, we adopt the color-based visual prompting scheme of Xie et al. [68] . Each face track is assigned a unique color, and its bounding boxes are drawn in that color on the raw video frames. The boxes are then referred to by color in the text prompt, allowing the MLLM to associate identities with their spatial locations.
blocks.zh: 以视觉特性提示 MLLM 。 我们没有向MLLM提供面轨的边框坐标,而是采用了谢等人的基于色的视觉提示方案. [68] (中文(简体) ). 每个面部音轨被分配到一个独特的颜色,其边框在原始视频框上以该颜色绘制. 然后在文本提示中以颜色来提及这些框,使MLLM能够将身份与其空间位置联系起来.

blocks.en: Prompting the MLLM with Visually Grounded Subtitles. Subtitles are embedded directly into the text prompt, with each speaker referred to by the color tag of their associated face track. We additionally include timestamps to enable more temporally accurate inference. For example, a line spoken by the character with blue face bounding boxes would be formatted as <693.2s> [BLUE] ‘‘Any idea who the girl in the black hat is?’’ <695.0s> .
blocks.zh: 以可视定位字幕提示 MLLM. 字幕直接嵌入到文本提示中,每个扬声器都以其相关面轨的颜色标记来称呼. 此外,我们还包括时间戳,以便能够作出更准确的时间推断。 例如,字符使用蓝色面框的行将格式化为<693.2s> [BLUE]知道那个戴黑帽子的女孩是谁吗? \<695.0s>。

blocks.en: Prompting the MLLM for Character Naming. Given the visual identities and visually grounded subtitles, we directly ask the MLLM to match each character name from the subtitles with a color, e.g., “ Which color corresponds to John Constantine? ” The color code thus bridges each visual identity’s spatial position to its corresponding name.
blocks.zh: 提示字符命名的 MLLM 。 鉴于视觉特征和视网膜字幕,我们直接要求MLLM将字幕中的每个字符名称配上颜色,例如“哪一种颜色与约翰·康斯坦丁相对应?” 因此,颜色代码将每个视觉特征的空间位置与相应的名称相连接。

blocks.en: 3.2 Fine-tuning the MLLM for Character Naming
blocks.zh: 3.2 精细调整字符命名的 MLLM

blocks.en: Following the prompting strategies described above, we adopt a two-stage R1-style fine-tuning recipe [ 22 ] to further improve the naming accuracy.
blocks.zh: 按照上述的促动策略,我们采用两阶段的R1型微调配方[22],以进一步提高命名精度.

blocks.en: Stage I: Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT). The first stage is a cold start that supervises the MLLM with synthetic reasoning traces. These traces are generated by a teacher MLLM, which is given the video frames, visually grounded subtitles, and ground-truth name-to-color mapping, and asked to produce a reasoning trace that leads to the correct answer. This teaches the student MLLM to follow the desired output format (i.e. a reasoning trace followed by the answer) before the reinforcement learning stage.
blocks.zh: 第一阶段:监督微调(SFT)。 第一阶段是一个冷酷的开始,以合成推理痕迹监督MLLM. 这些痕迹是由一位老师MLLM生成的,他得到了视频帧,视觉上下潜字幕,以及地面-真实姓名对颜色的映射,并被要求产生推理痕迹,从而得出正确的答案. 这使得学生MLLM在强化学习阶段之前遵循期望的输出格式(即一个推理跟踪,然后是答案).

blocks.en: A naive application of GRPO to this task suffers from a subtle shortcut: the model can latch onto color-specific cues. For instance, it may always associate the protagonist with “red” simply because “red” is the most frequently used color in the training distribution. We address this with a simple but effective color-permutation augmentation : during RL training, we randomly permute the color assignment for each sample. The ground-truth name–face mapping is invariant under such permutations, so consistent rewards across permuted variants are achievable only by reasoning about identity itself. This regularizes the policy toward color-agnostic reasoning and, empirically, accounts for a significant share of our gains over the cold-start baseline.
blocks.zh: GRPO对这项任务的天真应用有一个微妙的捷径:模型可以锁定特定颜色的提示. 例如,它可能总是将主角与“红色”联系在一起,因为“红色”是培训分发中最常用的颜色。 我们用一个简单但有效的色-增程来解决这个问题:在RL训练中,我们随机地给每个样本分配颜色。 地面真名-面部映射在这种布局下是变化无常的,因此,只有对身份本身进行推理,才能在各种变体中取得一致的回报。 这使色彩不可知推理政策正规化,并且从经验上讲,占我们相对于冷启动基线收益的很大一部分。

blocks.zh: 4 字符库建设的流线管道

blocks.en: 4.2 Error Correction during Character Bank Construction
blocks.zh: 4.2 字符库构建过程中的错误校正

blocks.en: The Markov structure of the update process ϕ ℬ \phi_{\mathcal{B}} makes it susceptible to error accumulation from upstream components (e.g. transcription, active-speaker detection, and identity grounding). To mitigate this, we introduce three error correction mechanisms deployed along the streaming chain. First, we use an MLLM to filter out noisy or ambiguous face tracks before clustering, ensuring high-quality embeddings. Second, we use an LLM to filter out query names from the subtitles that are unlikely to refer to on-screen characters. Third, we resolve cross-entry name conflicts after each shot using a greedy voting scheme that enforces one-to-one name assignment. Together, these mechanisms address distinct error modes and stabilize the evolution of ℬ t \mathcal{B}_{t} without revisiting past observations. We refer the reader to Appendix C for further details.

blocks.en: 5 Experiments
blocks.zh: 5 实验

blocks.en:
This section presents our evaluation. We first introduce the metrics (Sec. 5.1 ), then evaluate each task. Sec. 5.2 evaluates our character naming (CN) module on the MCN test set against state-of-the-art open- and closed-source models. Sec. 5.3 evaluates the full streaming character bank pipeline, measuring how well our method tracks each character’s first visual appearance and the first moment it can be linked to a name, and compares the final character bank against the IMDB ground truth.
We ablate key design choices, including the two-stage fine-tuning strategy and data augmentation for CN, and the error correction mechanisms for the character bank. Implementation details and ablations are provided in Appendix D and Appendix E .

本节介绍我们的评价。 我们首先提出衡量标准(第5.1条),然后评估每项任务。 第5.2条 对照最先进的开源和闭源模型,在MCN测试集上评价我们的角色命名(CN)模块. 第5.3sec. 评估全流字符库管道, 测量我们的方法如何追踪每个字符的第一次视觉外观,
我们放弃关键设计选择,包括CN的两阶段微调策略和数据增强,以及字符库的错误校正机制. 附录D和附录E载有执行细节和清单。

blocks.en: 5.1 Evaluation Metrics
blocks.zh: 5.1 评价计量

blocks.en: Character Naming Accuracy. We evaluate for two settings. Overall accuracy is computed over all name queries, including those labelled none when the mentioned character cannot be linked to any on-screen face track. Known accuracy is computed only over queries whose ground-truth label is a valid face track, thereby examining the model’s ability to correctly ground on-screen characters.

blocks.en: Character Bank Mean Temporal IoU. To evaluate the character bank streaming pipeline, we propose a Mean Temporal IoU (mTIoU) metric that measures how closely the bank tracks ground-truth human knowledge of each character over time.

blocks.en: 5.2 Results on Character Naming
blocks.zh: 5.2 字符命名结果

blocks.en: We evaluate Character Naming (CN) with three sets of methods. First, we compare against several baselines, including a random baseline that uniformly selects from the candidate colors, non-proprietary open-source MLLMs (Qwen3VL-4B-Thinking, Qwen3VL-8B-Instruct, and Qwen3.5-9B [ 2 ] ), and a naive fine-tuning baseline obtained by directly fine-tuning Qwen3VL-8B-Instruct on the MCN training set. Second, we report the result of our CN model, which is obtained by two-stage R1-style fine-tuning of Qwen3VL-4B-Thinking on the MCN training set. Third, we compare against state-of-the-art proprietary MLLMs: Gemini-3-Flash-Preview and Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview [ 19 ] . All models receive the same inputs with a visually prompted video clip, visually grounded subtitles, and queried character names, and are asked to output the corresponding box colors.
blocks.zh: 我们用三套方法评估字符命名。 首先,我们比较几个基线,包括从候选颜色中统一选择的随机基线,非专有的开源MLLMs(Qune3VL-4B-Thinking,Qune3VL-8B-Instruct,和Qune3.5-9B[2]),以及直接微调在MCN训练集上的Qune3VL-8B-Instruct获得的天真微调基线. 第二,我们报告我们的CN模型的结果,这是通过在MCN训练集上对Qune3VL-4B-Thinking进行两阶段的R1型微调得到的. 第三,我们比较最先进的专有MLLM:双子座-3-Flash-Preview和双子座3.1-Pro-Preview[19]. 所有模型都收到同样的输入,带有视觉激发的视频剪辑,视底字幕,并询问字符名称,并被要求输出相应的框颜色.

blocks.en: Discussion. Compared with open-source models such as Qwen3.5-9B, our two-stage fine-tuned model more accurately names characters in direct address scenarios (e.g. shot–reverse-shot, telephone conversations), better exploits visual cues (e.g. pointing, handshakes), and improves temporal grounding between subtitles and frames. A qualitative comparison is provided in Appendix I .
blocks.zh: 讨论。 与Quen3.5-9B等开源模型相比,我们两个阶段的微调模型在直接地址情景(如shot–verse-shot,电话交谈)中更准确的名字字符,更好地利用视觉提示(如指,握),改善字幕和帧之间的时间定位. 附录一提供了定性比较。

blocks.en: Nevertheless, a gap remains to the strongest proprietary model, likely driven by errors in transcription and active-speaker detection. We hypothesise that models such as Gemini [ 19 ] can partially recover from these errors by leveraging lip motion, whereas our model is more sensitive to such upstream noise.
blocks.zh: 然而,最强的专有模式仍存在差距,可能是由于抄写错误和主动语音检测。 我们假设双子座[19]这样的模型可以通过利用唇动来从这些错误中部分恢复,而我们的模型对这样的上游噪声更为敏感.

blocks.en: There are also cases where both Gemini [ 19 ] and our model fail. In particular, both struggle with (i) subtle cues (e.g. brief pointing among multiple characters), (ii) complex scenes with motion, and (iii) over-predicting on-screen characters when the ground-truth character is absent. We refer readers to Appendix I for further analysis of these failure modes.
blocks.zh: 也有双子座[19]和我们的模型都失败的情况. 特别是,两者都与(一) 微妙提示(例如,在多个人物中短暂指针),(二) 有动作的复杂场景,以及(三) 地面真实性缺失时在屏幕上过度预测人物. 我们请读者参阅附录一,进一步分析这些故障模式。

blocks.en: Evaluation on Unseen Movies. We also observe that proprietary models and pre-trained open-source models might have seen the movies that we test on. Therefore, they could infer the character identities without using cues from the clips but from their previous knowledge. This introduces a risk of data contamination, potentially leading to an overestimation of the models’ actual capabilities on our benchmark. To address this concern, we collect 102 102 manually annotated clips from four films released from March 2026 onward ( Voicemails for Isabelle , 19 June 2026; In the Grey , 15 May 2026; The Death of Robin Hood , 19 June 2026; Heartstopper Forever , 17 July 2026), after the reported training cut-offs of both Gemini-3.1-Pro (February 2026) and Qwen3-VL (September 2025), yielding 159 159 character-naming questions, 25 25 of which have none as the answer. Neither model can therefore have encountered these films during pre-training.
blocks.zh: 对不明电影的评价. 我们还观察到,专有模型和预先训练过的开源模型可能已经看过我们测试过的电影. 因此,他们可以推断角色身份,而不使用片段的提示,而是使用他们之前的知识. 这带来了数据污染的风险,有可能导致高估模型在基准上的实际能力。 为了解决这一问题,我们从2026年3月上映的四部电影中收集了102个手动附加说明的剪辑(Voicemail for Isabelle 2026年6月19日;In the Grey 2026年5月15日;The Robin Hood 2026年6月19日;Heartstopper Forever 2026年7月17日),在双子座-3.1-Pro(2026年2月)和Qune3-VL(2025年9月)的训练截断报告之后,产生了159个159个字符命名问题,其中25个没有答案. 因此,在预训期间,这两个模型都不可能遇到这些电影。

blocks.en: In Tab. 3 , the relative ordering of methods from Tab. 2 is unchanged on both metrics. Our fine-tuned 4B model again outperforms all open-source baselines by a wide margin and trails only the proprietary Gemini models. blocks.en: For streaming character bank construction, we use Gemini-3-Flash-Preview and Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview [ 19 ] as baselines, prompting them to output each character’s name, first visual occurrence timestamp, and first naming timestamp. To obtain face clusters, we ask the models to identify timestamps with close-up or clear solo shots, from which we perform face detection, extract features, and cluster faces, selecting the largest connected component as the predicted cluster. As these models are not designed to directly output face crops or clusters, we consider a prediction correct if any face in the cluster matches the ground-truth identity.
blocks.zh: 对于流体字符库建设,我们使用双子座-3-Flash-Preview和双子座3.1-Pro-Preview[19]作为基线,促使它们输出每个字符的名字,第一个视觉发生时间戳,以及第一个命名时间戳. 为了获得面团,我们要求模型识别带有特写或清晰的独奏镜头的时标,我们从中进行面团检测,提取特征,以及团团面,选择最大的连接组件作为预测的团团. 由于这些模型的设计不是为了直接输出作物或集群,我们认为,如果集群中的任何表面都与地面真实身份相符,那么预测是正确的。

blocks.en: Results. As shown in Tab. 4 , our pipeline substantially outperforms both proprietary baselines across all metrics, despite operating in the more challenging streaming setting. These improvements reflect more accurate identification of when characters first appear and are named (mTIoU), as well as stronger alignment of the final character bank with canonical identities from external sources (PCR). These gains are especially notable given that the baselines have full-movie access while ours processes the video in a single streaming pass. Appendix J shows two examples of the final constructed character bank.
blocks.zh: 结果。 如图4所示,尽管在更具挑战性的流水环境中运作,但我们的管道在所有指标上都大大超过专有基线。 这些改进反映了更准确地识别人物首次出现和被命名的时间(mTIoU),以及最终字符库与来自外部来源(PCR)的犬科特征更加一致. 这些进展尤其显著,因为基线可全程使用,而我们的视频则在单一的流传通道中处理。 附 录 J显示两个最终构建字符库的例子.

blocks.en: Discussion. Our pipeline performs well on movies such as Juno and Meet the Parents , which feature relatively simple scenes with few participants and a limited set of recurring characters. In these cases, identity clustering is generally reliable, aided by our face-track filtering. Even when Character Naming errors occur, our method can often recover as additional evidence emerges over time.
blocks.zh: 讨论。 我们的管道在诸如朱诺(Juno)和"见父母"(Meet the Parents)等电影上表现良好, 在这种情况下,身份组合一般是可靠的,通过我们的面轨过滤得到帮助. 即使在"字符命名"错误发生时,我们的方法也常常可以随着时间推移出现额外证据而恢复.

blocks.en: Performance degrades, however, in movies with many scenes containing numerous minor or background characters. In Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire , for example, background characters introduce noise into clustering, which distracts the Character Naming process. Movies with very large named casts, such as Four Weddings and a Funeral , with over 50 50 named characters among hundreds of recurring faces, are also particularly challenging, as the model must maintain and disambiguate many identities over long temporal contexts.
blocks.zh: 然而,在电影中表演会退化,许多场景中包含着众多的次要或背景人物. 例如在"哈利·波特"(Harry Potter)和"火之歌"(Goblet of Fire)中,背景人物将噪音引入集群,这分散了角色命名过程的注意力. 电影具有非常大的名字铸造,例如四婚礼和葬礼,在数百张反复出现的脸孔中,有50多个名字的人物,这些电影也具有特别的挑战性,因为模型必须维持许多身份,并在长时间内使其脱落。

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en: Character-Centric Movie Understanding. Movie understanding has emerged as a milestone task for video understanding, owing to its long temporal span and rich multimodal narrative structure, motivating a variety of datasets [ 28 , 60 , 3 , 55 , 61 ] . A representative line of research is Audio Description (AD) generation [ 48 , 25 , 24 , 26 , 68 , 67 , 31 , 21 ] , where Han et al. [24] identifies character recognition as central to the task. Existing work typically takes one of two shortcuts: relying on curated sources like IMDB cast lists [ 43 , 25 , 24 , 26 , 68 , 67 ] or fan wikis [ 21 ] , which are often incomplete or unavailable for new films, or sidestepping naming entirely with placeholders like “Person A” [ 18 , 75 , 56 ] . A separate line of work links names to faces directly from video. Early approaches align shooting scripts with subtitles for weak labels and use active-speaker detection to associate them with face tracks [ 15 , 54 ] . Extensions add probabilistic models over face, speech, and clothing cues [ 58 ] , coreference resolution [ 45 ] , and script-free dialogue-based naming for recurring TV casts [ 27 , 41 , 12 ] . A complementary line assumes identities are known and analyses interactions via gaze and eyelines [ 37 , 36 , 20 , 46 ] . We revisit this problem in the era of MLLMs. Prior dialogue-based approaches, including Haurilet et al. [27] , cast naming as an optimisation over many mentions across clips or episodes of a recurring TV cast; we instead resolve identity from the single clip surrounding the name as a human viewer does, generalising to feature-length movies in the wild where names are typically mined from one-off dialogue. In concurrent work, Pu et al. [44] track identities via textual appearance descriptions, a lossy representation that fails to distinguish visually similar characters and degrades under costume or lighting changes. Our character bank instead grounds each identity in visual exemplars, retaining the fine-grained cues text abstracts away.

blocks.en: Visual Reasoning in Vision-Language Models (MLLMs). Recent work extends reasoning from Large Language Models (LLMs) [ 65 , 32 ] to the multimodal setting. Early approaches prompt frozen MLLMs to produce intermediate reasoning steps [ 62 , 39 ] , while more recent methods train explicit reasoning via reinforcement learning. Inspired by [ 22 ] , Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been adapted to MLLMs, showing that RL with verifiable rewards improves reasoning ability [ 51 , 29 , 74 , 38 ] , including across perception tasks such as detection [ 35 ] , segmentation [ 34 ] , and fine-grained perception [ 72 ] . For video understanding specifically, prior work incorporates temporal reasoning into this paradigm, e.g. via temporal-aware GRPO [ 16 ] , joint spatio-temporal reasoning [ 33 ] , and long-form temporal grounding [ 63 ] . In parallel, visual prompting introduces structured cues, such as colored masks [ 69 ] , boxes [ 53 , 6 ] , region tokens [ 10 , 71 ] , or identity markers [ 68 ] , to link visual entities with language. Our approach builds on both lines of work, combining color-based visual prompting with a two-stage SFT + GRPO fine-tuning strategy to enable an MLLM to reason about character identity from visual and dialogue cues jointly.
blocks.zh: 视觉-语言模型中的视觉理性(MLLMs). 最近的工作将推理从大语言模型(LLMs)[65,32]延伸至多式联运设置. 早期的方法促使冻结的MLLMs产生中间推理步骤[62,39],而较新的方法通过强化学习来训练明确的推理. 受到[22]的启发,集团相对政策优化(GRPO)被改编为MLLMs,显示具有可核查奖励的RL提高了推理能力[51,29,74,38],包括跨感知任务,如检测[35],分化[34],以及精细的感知[72]. 就视频理解而言,先前的工作将时间推理纳入这一范式,例如通过时间意识的GRPO[16],联合时空推理[33],以及长式时间定位[63]。 同时,视觉提示引入了结构化的提示,如彩色口罩[69],盒子[53,6],区域标志[10,71],或身份标记[68],将视觉实体与语言联系起来. 我们的方法基于两条工作线,将基于色彩的视觉提示与两阶段的SFT + GRPO微调策略结合起来,使MLLM能够从视觉和对话提示中对人物身份进行推理.

blocks.en:
Person Clustering in Long Videos. Grouping person appearances by identity is a long-standing problem in video understanding, with applications to cast listing, character-based browsing, and story understanding [ 17 , 11 , 15 , 59 ] .
Early work focuses on face clustering , using metric or representation learning to group face tracks under variations in pose, lighting, and expression [ 50 , 64 , 70 , 52 ] . These methods exploit spatio-temporal structure in edited videos via co-occurrence constraints [ 4 , 30 , 66 ] , or apply nearest-neighbor clustering over pretrained embeddings [ 49 , 42 ] . However, they rely on visible faces, limiting performance when characters are occluded, off-screen, or viewed from behind.
To address this, Brown et al. [5] introduce Video Person-Clustering, grouping face, body, and voice cues via multimodal hierarchical clustering, with later work extending this direction using graph-based formulations [ 40 ] .
Our pipeline follows a similar multimodal approach, using face embeddings as the primary signal with voice as fallback. Unlike prior work, we operate in a streaming setting, where clusters are instantiated, updated, and named as the film unfolds, extending online clustering [ 1 , 7 ] to feature-length videos.
blocks.zh:
长视频中的人物集群. 按身份分组人物的出现是视频理解中长期存在的问题,有投影上市的应用,人物浏览,故事理解[17,11,15,59].
早期工作的重点是脸谱组合,利用衡量或表现方面的学习,在姿势、照明和表情变化下组合面谱[50、64、70、52]。 这些方法利用经编辑的视频中的时空结构,通过共同发生限制[4、30、66],或在预先训练的嵌入物上采用近邻组合[49、42]。 然而,他们依靠可见的面孔,当角色被占据,关闭屏幕,或者从后面观看时,限制性能.
为了解决这个问题,Brown等人。 [5] 通过多式联运等级集群,引入视频人物组合,分组面,身体,和语音提示,后期工作采用图表化配体[40]扩展这一方向.
我们的管道采用类似的多式联运方法,将面部嵌入作为主要信号,声音反射。 与之前的工作不同,我们运行在一个流媒体的设定中,集群被即时化,更新,并被命名为电影的展开,将在线集群[1,7]扩展至特征长度的视频.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion
blocks.zh: 7 讨论情况

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduce the task of Character Naming from dialogue and close the gap between open-source models and the best proprietary models. Building on this task, we further introduce a streaming pipeline to construct a character bank , enabling online, human-like movie understanding. For both tasks, we compare our method with Gemini [ 19 ] , though neither task is fully solved, even by proprietary models. A natural next step is to develop models or an agentic framework to overcome the current failure modes, and thereby improve performance.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们介绍了从对话中命名字符的任务,并缩小开源模型与最佳专有模型之间的差距. 在这项任务的基础上,我们进一步引入了一条流畅的管道来构建一个人物库,从而能够实现在线的,人性化的电影理解. 对于这两个任务,我们比较了我们的方法和双子座[19],虽然两个任务都没有完全解决,即使是通过专有模型. 下一个自然步骤是开发模型或代理框架,以克服目前的失败模式,从而提高性能。

blocks.en: Face-Track Filtering. Prior to clustering, we introduce an MLLM-based filtering stage to discard unreliable or ambiguous face tracks, thereby maintaining clean and identifiable clusters in the bank. This step removes low-quality observations, including blurred faces and extreme profile views. Empirically, embeddings derived from the retained high-quality tracks are sufficiently stable, rendering clustering errors negligible under our operating thresholds.
blocks.zh: 面轨过滤. 在分组之前,我们引入基于MLLM的过滤阶段,以丢弃不可靠或模棱两可的面孔轨迹,从而在银行中保持清洁和可识别的集群. 这一步骤消除了低质量的观测,包括模糊的面部和极端的剖面观点. 经验是,从保留下来的高质量轨道中衍生出来的嵌入足够稳定,使我们的运行阈值下集群错误可以忽略不计.

blocks.en: Query Name Filtering. As previously discussed, when no on-screen character actually corresponds to the candidate name, both our model and Gemini tend to over-assign one of the visible faces to an off-screen name rather than abstaining. To circumvent this, we filter the candidate name pool upstream so that off-screen names rarely reach the naming step in the first place. Concretely, we use an LLM (Qwen3.5-9B) to inspect each subtitle window and keep only those candidate names likely to refer to a character currently on screen. This requires reasoning over the flow of the surrounding dialogue rather than classifying each line in isolation, since whether a named person is actually present or merely being discussed is rarely decidable from a single utterance.
blocks.zh: 查询名称过滤 。 如前所述,当没有屏幕上的角色实际上与候选名字相对应时,我们的模型和双子座都倾向于将一个可见的面孔过度分配给一个屏幕外的名字,而不是弃权. 为了规避这一点,我们先向上游过滤候选名称池,这样,不筛选名称就很少到达命名步骤. 具体来说,我们使用一个LLM(Quen3.5-9B)来检查每个字幕窗口,只保留那些可能指向当前屏幕上的字符的候选人名. 这就需要对周围对话的流向进行推理,而不是孤立地对每一行进行分类,因为一个被点名的人是否确实在场或只是被讨论,很少从单一的言论中决定。

blocks.en: Inter-Entry Name Disambiguation. Ideally, each name should be uniquely associated with a single entry; however, MLLM-induced errors can lead to conflicts across entries. We resolve these after each shot using a greedy voting procedure: for names assigned to multiple entries, the entry with the highest vote retains the name, while others revert to their next-best candidates. This process is repeated until convergence.
blocks.zh: 异名异义. 理想的情况是,每个名称都应该与单一条目有独特的关联;然而,MLLM引起的错误可能导致条目间的冲突. 我们用一个贪婪的投票程序在每次投票后解决这些问题:对于分配给多个条目的名字,得票最高的条目保留该名称,而其他人则恢复其次优候选人. 这一过程在趋同之前反复进行。

blocks.en: Overall, these mechanisms address complementary failure modes in the streaming process and prevent error accumulation as ℬ t \mathcal{B}_{t} evolves, without requiring access to past observations.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这些机制处理流化过程中互补的故障模式,并随着B t\ mathcal{B}_{t}的演化防止错误积累,而不需要访问过去的观测.

blocks.en: Appendix F Additional Baseline for Streaming Character Bank Construction
blocks.zh: 附录F 流动字符银行建设的补充基线

blocks.en: In Sec. 5.3 , we use Gemini-3-Flash-Preview and Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview [ 19 ] as baselines for streaming character bank construction. We note that these baselines are disadvantaged by our requirement that they emit face exemplars, a form of output they are not designed to produce. No existing method targets this setting directly: prior work either presupposes a pre-built character bank or assumes a recurring television cast. Proprietary MLLMs are therefore the closest available point of comparison, notwithstanding the mismatch in output format. The lenient scoring criterion was adopted to compensate that.
blocks.zh: 在5.3sec.中,我们使用双子座-3-Flash-Preview和双子座3.1-Pro-Preview[19]作为流体字符库建设的基线. 我们注意到,这些基线因我们要求它们发出实例而处于不利地位,而这种产出形式不是设计用来生产的。 目前没有一种方法直接针对这种设置:前期工作要么预先假定预先建成的字符库,要么假设电视反复播映. 因此,专有的MLLMs是目前最接近的比较点,尽管产出格式不匹配。 为了补偿这一点,采用了宽大评分标准。

blocks.en: To provide a comparison that does not rely on lenient scoring to compensate for the output-format mismatch, we have additionally implemented a classical weakly-supervised baseline [ 27 ] . It uses exactly the same face tracking, clustering, and majority-vote name binding as our pipeline, replacing only the mechanism by which names are linked to faces, and is given access to the full film rather than operating in a streaming pass. The weakly-supervised baseline uses subtitle text alone, with no audio, no pixels, and no vision-language model. A character vocabulary is extracted from the transcript by NER, and each mention is typed as first-, second-, or third-person using the five grammar rules in [ 27 ] , so that first- and second-person mentions ("I’m Harry", "Hello, Harry") imply presence while third-person mentions ("Where is Harry?") imply absence. Each typed mention yields a positive or negative bag of face tracks from a surrounding window, here three shots centred on the mention’s shot. A per-character linear MIL model (Normalized Set Kernel, the best-performing solver in [ 27 ] ) is trained on InsightFace embeddings, and a second-stage classifier, trained on each model’s most confident tracks, scores every track in the film and assigns the argmax name.
blocks.zh: 为了提供一种不依赖宽大评分来弥补产出格式不匹配的比较,我们额外实施了传统的弱监督基线[27]。 它使用与我们的管道完全相同的面部跟踪,集群,和多数选票名称绑定,仅取代了名字与面部连接的机制,并被赋予了全片的通道,而不是在流传的通道中运行. 弱监督基线仅使用字幕文本,没有音频,像素,也没有视觉语言模型. NER从笔录中提取一个人物词汇,每一次提及都用[27]中的五种语法规则打成第一,第二,第三人称,因此第一和第二人称("我是哈利","你好,哈利")意味着存在,而第三人称("哈利在哪里?")则意味着缺席. 每一次打字都会产生一袋正面或负面的脸迹, 每个字符的线性MIL模型(Normalized Set Kernel,[27]中表现最好的解析器)接受过InsightFace嵌入式的训练,以及一个第二阶段的分类器,接受过每个模型最自信的轨迹的训练,在胶片中给每个轨迹打分,并指定了agmax名称.

blocks.en: MovieNet [ 28 ] provides body bounding-box annotations on sparse 240P keyframes indexed by ( s , k ) (s,k) , a shot index and within-shot image index. These indices do not identify frames in the native-resolution movie file, and MovieNet’s shot segmentation does not coincide with ours. To build the MCN dataset, we must (i) recover the exact frame number f ⋆ ∈ { 0 , … , N − 1 } f^{\star}\!\in\!\{0,\dots,N{-}1\} in the full video for each annotated keyframe, and (ii) rescale every box from 240P to native resolution. We address this with a three-stage coarse-to-fine pipeline: CLIP retrieval for coarse localisation, longest-increasing-subsequence (LIS) filtering to remove inconsistent matches, and perceptual hashing for exact frame recovery.

blocks.en: CLIP Feature Extraction. For every MovieNet keyframe and for every 24th frame ( ≈ \approx 1 fps at 24 fps) of each full-resolution video, we extract a 512-D CLIP ViT-B/32 image embedding. The keyframes form a query pool 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} and the video samples a source pool 𝒮 \mathcal{S} . Both pools are cached per movie so that the subsequent stages run independently per title.

blocks.en: Coarse Alignment via FAISS Retrieval and LIS Filtering. Within each movie we run exact L2 nearest-neighbor search (FAISS IndexFlatL2 ) of every query against 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and take the top-1 source frame as a coarse anchor f ^ i \widehat{f}_{i} for keyframe i i . CLIP retrieval is robust to the resolution gap and to codec and color differences between annotation crops and rendered video frames, but it occasionally returns a visually similar shot from elsewhere in the movie. We prune such errors by exploiting the fact that MovieNet keyframes are listed in temporal order: the sequence ( f ^ i ) i (\widehat{f}_{i})_{i} must be monotonically increasing. We compute its longest increasing subsequence in O ⁡ ( n ​ log ⁡ n ) O(n\log n) and mark every keyframe outside the LIS as unreliable ( f ^ i ← − 1 \widehat{f}_{i}\!\leftarrow\!-1 ). The criterion is strict but conservative: any rogue match must drop out of the LIS together with whichever neighbor it conflicts with, and the LIS retains the longer consistent chain.

blocks.en: Fig. 5 shows six representative annotations from the MCN dataset, drawn from films that span genres, eras, and visual styles — from the period crowds of Gangs of New York to the romantic comedy of Sleepless in Seattle , the political drama of The Ides of March , and the sports biopic Moneyball . This diversity is by design: a character-naming benchmark that generalizes beyond a single genre or production style must capture the full range of cinematographic conventions through which characters are introduced.
blocks.zh: 图5显示了来自MCN数据集的6个代表性说明,这些说明来自跨流派,时代和视觉风格的电影——从纽约的帮派的人群时期到西雅图的浪漫喜剧"无眠",政治剧"三月的偶像",以及体育生理学钱球. 这种多样性是通过设计实现的:一般化超越单一流派或制作风格的人物命名基准,必须捕捉人物通过的各种电影惯例.

blocks.en: The examples also illustrate the variety of cues a model must exploit to resolve a name to the correct face. The most common case is direct address , in which one character names another in dialogue, but the visual realisation of this act is far from uniform. The named character may be identified through the canonical shot–reverse-shot structure, through an eyeline match when speaker and addressee share the frame, or through a telephone conversation where the named character is entirely off-screen at the moment of naming and must be linked to a face seen elsewhere in the clip. A separate class of examples requires reasoning from on-screen text : the character’s name appears as a written cue — a name tag, a letter, a sign, or a screen — and the model must perform OCR and then ground the recovered string to the correct visual identity. Cases like these are unsolvable from dialogue alone and require multimodal reasoning over both spoken and written language alongside visual evidence.
blocks.zh: 这些例子还表明,一个模型必须利用各种提示,才能解决一个名字的正确面孔。 最常见的情况是直接地址,其中一个角色在对话中指另一个角色,但这一行为的视觉实现远非统一. 被命名的人物可以通过canonic shot–反射结构来识别,在扬声器和收件人共享帧时通过眼线匹配,或者通过电话交谈来识别,在命名时被命名的人物是完全不屏蔽的,必须和剪辑中其他地方看到的面孔联系起来. 一个单独的类例需要从屏幕上文本中推理:人物的名字作为书面提示出现——一个名字标记,一个字母,一个符号,或者一个屏幕——模型必须执行OCR,然后将恢复的字符串打到正确的视觉身份. 此类案件仅靠对话是无法解决的,需要结合视觉证据对口头和书面语言进行多式联运推理。

blocks.en: Qualitative Examples. Fig. 6 shows three representative examples covering the main cue types our model handles: direct address , where a speaker calls another character by name; third-party reference , where a name is mentioned about someone else in the scene; and visual reasoning , where the spoken cue is ambiguous and the mapping must be inferred from scene role. In each case, our model grounds the name to the correct colored box by jointly leveraging the spoken cue and the surrounding visual context.
blocks.zh: 定性例. 图6显示三个涵盖我们模型手柄的主要提示类型的代表性例子:直接地址,一个发言者用名字称呼另一个字符;第三方参考,在现场提到另一个人的名字;视觉推理,在现场的提示含糊不清,必须从场景角色推断出地图。 在每一种情况下,我们的模型都通过共同利用口语提示和周围的视觉环境,将名字引向正确的彩色框。

blocks.en: Comparing with Baseline. We compare our output against a strong baseline on the same scene in Fig. 7 . Our model produces a concise, well-grounded explanation and arrives at the correct identity, whereas the baseline generates a long chain of thought with repeated self-verifications yet commits to an incorrect mapping. Longer reasoning traces do not guarantee better grounding: our model achieves more accurate association with substantially fewer tokens.
blocks.zh: 与基线相比较。 我们把我们的产出与菲格同一场景的有力基线进行比较。 7 (英语). 我们的模型提出了简明、理由充分的解释,并得出正确的特征,而基线则产生一长串思维,反复进行自我核查,但却承诺进行不正确的绘图。 较长的推理痕迹并不能保证更好的立足点:我们的模式实现更准确的联系,而代号则要少得多。

blocks.en: Failure Cases. We analyse representative failure cases of our model and Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview in Fig. 8 and Fig. 9 . Fig. 8 shows cases where Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview fails despite being the strongest proprietary baseline, suggesting that it can struggle to use subtle visual actions and interactions that are crucial for character naming. Fig. 9 further compares common failure modes across both models. Overall, our model appears better at leveraging fine-grained visual cues, speaker activity, and cross-turn dialogue context, while remaining errors are often caused by subtle actions, ambiguous speaker grounding, or noisy subtitles.
blocks.zh: 失败案例。 我们分析我们模型和双子座3.1-Pro-Preview在图8和图9中的代表性故障案例. 图8显示双子座3.1-Pro-Preview尽管是最强的专利基线却失败的案例,这表明它可以努力使用对于人物命名至关重要的微妙视觉动作和互动. 图9进一步比较了两种模式的常见故障模式. 总体来说,我们的模式似乎更能利用精细的视觉提示、演讲者活动和交叉对话背景,而剩余的错误往往由微妙行动、含糊的演讲者地面或吵闹的字幕造成。

blocks.en: Figure 6: Qualitative results for character naming. We associate character names with their facial appearances in movies, mirroring how audiences infer who is who while watching. Characters may be introduced through diverse cues, including direct address by other characters (top), visual reasoning with common knowledge (middle), and third-party reference (bottom). In each case, the model grounds the name to the correct colored box by combining the spoken cue with visual evidence such as gaze, gesture, and scene role. Correctly linking character identities is central to movie understanding, enabling coherent character tracking across scenes. The examples are taken from Sleepless in Seattle , Four Weddings and a Funeral and Meet the Parents .

blocks.en: Figure 7: Comparison of reasoning efficiency on character naming. We compare our model against Qwen3.5-9B on the same scene. Our model produces a concise, well-grounded answer that directly links the spoken cue (“Congratulations, Walter”) to visual evidence (gaze and handshake direction), correctly identifying the orange box as Walter. In contrast, the baseline generates a lengthy chain of thought with repeated re-examinations and self-verifications, yet arrives at an incorrect mapping (green). This illustrates that longer reasoning does not guarantee better grounding: our model achieves more accurate character naming with substantially fewer tokens.

blocks.en: We present qualitative results for streaming character bank construction on two films, Juno and Meet the Parents . As shown in Fig. 10 , our pipeline constructs clean character entries for the major characters in Juno , grouping representative face tracks and linking them to canonical names while also preserving discovered aliases. Fig. 11 shows a second example on Meet the Parents . The bank again identifies the most prominent characters, but also reveals typical failure cases in complex multi-person scenes, where ambiguous visual context and transcription errors can lead to incorrect or noisy name bindings. These examples demonstrate that the proposed bank construction procedure is effective across different films, while remaining errors are primarily due to challenging name evidence rather than face-track clustering. Moreover, we refer readers to the supplementary video, which shows the full streaming character bank construction process for Juno.
blocks.zh: 我们为两部电影, 如图10所示,我们的管道为朱诺的主要人物构建了干净的字符条目,将代表性的面迹轨迹分组,并将其与犬形名称联系起来,同时保留已发现的别名. 图11显示了关于“见父母”的第二个例子。 该银行再次识别出最突出的人物,但也揭示了复杂多人场景中的典型失败案例,其中模糊的视觉上下文和抄写错误可能导致名字绑定不正确或吵闹. 这些例子表明,拟议的银行建造程序在不同电影中是有效的,而其余的错误主要是名字证据有挑战性,而不是面轨组合。 此外,我们请读者参考补充视频,该视频展示了朱诺的全流字符库建设过程.

blocks.en:
Our method identifies characters in movies using cinematic and dialogue cues. This technique can be used to generate accurate audio descriptions and speaker-attributed subtitles, improving accessibility for audiences with visual or hearing impairments.
This method does not perform open-world face recognition or release any identity gallery from personal video sources. We therefore do not foresee significant negative societal impacts from this work.
blocks.zh:
我们的方法用电影和对话提示来识别电影中的人物。 这一技术可用于生成准确的音频描述和演讲者属性字幕,改善视力或听力障碍的受众的无障碍环境.
这种方法不进行开放世界面部识别,也不发布个人视频来源的任何身份画廊. 因此,我们预计这项工作不会产生重大的负面社会影响。
